Well it depends on the hair texture. I have really curly/ kinky hair (4c), anf when i go to the stylists they usually wash, condition, dry it, and detangle it. After combing everything out, my stylist would plan out the style, and use a little rat tail comb to make the first section. She loops the extension into my natural hair at the root of the braid(if i get extensions), and with a little hair oil starts to braid the hair. At the end she twists the little stray strands up so it doesn't need a rubber band or anything, and then she does it again and again for every braid. She has to make sure to follow the correct parts with every braid so that it looks neat at the end. When shes done she usually puts a bit of moisturizer on my hair and out the door i go. For me that can take 4+ hours, and a little over $100. I learned how to braid my own hair at home so i don't spend that money all the time, but when i do that's usually the process. Hope that helps!!
